checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that body-level checkpoints (tail, hind limbs, overall slenderness) are untestable due to the tight cropping of the image. The verdicts for visible facial features (bare face, eyes, nose, ruff) are accurate and supported by visual evidence. The Router was not too lenient; it strictly required full visibility for a 'present' verdict.
artifact_review:
The Router found no artifacts. The Perceptual Quality Auditor confirmed no graphics-level distortions (blur, noise). The Topology Boundary Auditor found a clean mask with high confidence, indicating no significant edge bleeding or fragmentation. However, the Animal Pose Auditor reported a HIGH artifact risk (82% low-confidence keypoints). 

CRITICAL INTERPRETATION: The low-confidence keypoints correspond almost entirely to body parts that are OCCLUDED or OUT OF FRAME (ears hidden by ruff, shoulders/limbs cropped out). According to the Reflector guidelines, low confidence due to occlusion/cropping is a WEAK signal and should be ignored if no visual anomalies are present. Visually, the visible head structure is sound. Therefore, I disagree with treating this as a structural defect. It is a false positive driven by domain shift and cropping. No new artifacts were found.
alignment_reasoning: The fine_grained_classifier strongly confirms the class 'guenon' (Logit 8.39 vs 5.08 for next best). All testable facial checkpoints (bare face, eye color, nose shape, ruff) are perfectly met. The image is a high-fidelity representation of the target class within the constraints of the crop.
artifact_reasoning: No visual artifacts detected. High-frequency fur details are sharp and realistic. Boundaries are clean. The high 'risk' from the pose auditor is dismissed because the low-confidence joints correspond to occluded/cropped regions (ears, limbs), not visible structural failures. The image is structurally sound for the visible portion.
